as_told.title: Aztec crash dismissed as hoax; Steinman's book and the Ramseys' rehabilitation

plain: The story is that a craft crashed near Aztec, New Mexico, around 1948, and that the case was then called a hoax in the early 1950s. The researcher Richard Dolan tells Michels he believes it, calling it the first crash case ever written about, and names the people around it: the writer Frank Scully, JP Cahn, Richard Geldreich, William Steinman, who he says wrote 'a really big fat book on it,' and Scott and Suzanne Ramsey, who he credits with rehabilitating the case, even though, he notes, Wikipedia still labels it a hoax.
